logic.note: Sounds while the pin toggles between 20 Hz and 20 kHz; silent on a steady level. Each new tone (start, or pitch change > 1 %) is counted and its note name recorded.

timing.note: The frequency is measured from the cycle-exact period of the edges on the pin (tone() timer interrupts, analogWrite PWM), sampled every 1 ms of virtual time. Tones shorter than 1 ms are not counted.

analog.note: Loudness is a relative 0..1 from the drive amplitude and a resonance curve around resonantHz (4 kHz). Electrically a 10 kΩ load (a real piezo is a ~20 nF capacitor: tiny average current, current spikes on each edge). No audio output.

emulates: Pitch from tone() and PWM, note names and melody history
doesNotEmulate: Harmonics and the timbre of a square wave
Magnetic (coil) passive buzzers, which draw 30–100 mA and need a transistor
testOnRealDevice: Loudness at the notes you use (piezos are quiet far below their resonance)
That your buzzer really is passive: an active one beeps at its own pitch on DC
